Vey's purse of play-crowns is fatter this time, and so is her suspicion.|The turnip market again. Vey walks the stalls with her purse and the expression of a duchess at a bad auction.} {Your neighbour's turnip is already a very convincing tiara.|Somebody's ruby is dripping slightly.|{season == "autumn": The turnips are fresh from Old Maud's patch and smell of earth.|The hall smells overwhelmingly of turnip.}} Make it dazzle {Your turnip becomes a sapphire the size of an egg. Vey turns it over, sniffs it, and pays three play-crowns. "It smells of turnip," she says. "I'll allow it."|You turn it into a golden pear. Vey bites it, which is cheating, then pays anyway, laughing.|Your turnip becomes a pocket watch that ticks. Vey listens to it and pays you double. "You made me want it," she says. "That's the whole art."} {Your jewel flickers back into a turnip as Vey reaches for it. The whole hall sees. Vey pays you one play-crown, out of pity.|Your sapphire has roots. Vey points this out, delighted, to everyone.|Your watch ticks, then sprouts leaves. "Charming," says Vey, and moves on.} Buy, and catch the fakes {You're given a few play-crowns and set loose as a customer. You catch three turnips in disguise by their smell. Vey nods. "The other half of the art."|You haggle your way down the stalls and catch the dripping ruby out. Its maker sulks.|You can tell a glamoured turnip at ten paces now. Vey makes you her assistant buyer for the rest of the hour.}

results.excerpt:
Pick a Card
Professor Vey's glamour lesson is a card game. Each student glamours a plain card to look like the queen of stars, and Vey picks out the true queen from the pile. Nobody, she says, has ever made her pick wrong. "Fool me, and you may skip the essay."
